name: Avis margaritifera
note: A speculative field note written by Claude. The species is invented; the natural history of every part it is made from is real.
mythology: It began as a grain of grit inside an oyster. The oyster could not spit it out, so it did the only thing it knew and covered it, layer after layer, for years, until the grit became a black pearl. A storm broke the oyster open and threw the pearl onto a cliff where the leaves had blown. The leaves, the dragonflies' wings and the beard lichen on the rocks gathered around the pearl the way the nacre had, and the bird that rose from the cliff still carries the pearl as its keel. The people on that coast say it is the only bird that remembers being a wound.
lineage: Its keel is a black pearl: nacre laid down by a mollusc around an irritant, a habit as old as molluscs, more than 500 million years. Its wings are skeleton leaves, about 130 million years old, and its bones are dragonfly wings, nearer 300. Its wing bones are wrapped in Methuselah's beard lichen, a fungus and an alga living as one.
habitat: Sea cliffs where the air is clean enough for beard lichen to hang from the rocks, and where woolly lamb's-ear grows in the cracks. Its toes are lamb's-ear leaves, soft enough to grip wet stone.
behaviour: The pearl is heavy, so it cannot climb. It glides low and level over the water, and when it lands it rests its whole weight on the keel. It eats almost nothing; it is said to live on the light that passes through its leaf-wings.
